title: Security and Compliance: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Security and Compliance: Visual Guide

1. Five Control Questions | four things already built in this course — an Analytics Hub listing, a BigLake table over GCS, a Dataflow streaming job, a RAG corpus — each tapped to reveal the five security questions it forces and the consequence of leaving each unanswered | the five mechanisms answer DIFFERENT questions (IAM authorises the request, Organization Policy rejects the configuration, KMS controls the key, Sensitive Data Protection controls the values, the hierarchy controls repetition), and most wrong answers are a correct mechanism aimed at the wrong question

2. Grant At Which Level | a 12-resource estate (org, prod/dev folders, ingest-prod and analytics-prod projects, raw/curated/published datasets, tables) with a role selector and an attachment-point selector recomputing the blast radius and how many PII resources are exposed | the attachment point is as important as the role — the same BigQuery Data Viewer at the prod folder reaches the raw PII dataset and at the curated dataset reaches nothing sensitive — and Token Creator on a service account reaches whatever that identity reaches, which is why impersonation is an access path

3. Envelope And Rotation | twelve months of data each wrapped by the key version primary when it was written, with a Google-managed vs CMEK mode toggle and rotate / disable / destroy actions recomputing how many months stay readable | default encryption is real encryption and CMEK buys control, rotation creates a new primary for NEW writes while old versions stay required to decrypt old data, disabling is a reversible central switch and destroying is crypto-shredding

4. Choose The Transform | five detected fields (email, phone, government ID, birth date, customer id) crossed with seven de-identification transforms, showing before/after plus verdict chips for analytical utility, re-identification, joins preserved and frequency leak | the transform is chosen from the analytical purpose, not from a security dial — masking to the last four characters suits customer service and not public release, date shifting keeps intervals, and deterministic tokenization preserves joins while still leaking frequency

5. Trace The Path | ten hops that carry data — primary tables, derived tables, caches, backups, DR copy, log exports, metadata, KMS key ring, an orchestrator's external API call, human access — each toggled inside or outside the boundary, with an Organization Policy location-constraint switch marking which hops a guardrail could even cover | residency is a location and sovereignty is the regime around it, so the claim is only as strong as the weakest hop, and a location constraint prevents creation of unsupported resources without moving existing data or validating external destinations
